title: Rewriting Text in My Own Writing Style
tools: QLoRA (quantized low-rank adaptation) · DPO (direct preference optimization) · vLLM · Qwen3.5-9B / Qwen3.8-27B · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster
blurb: I did a QLoRA (quantized low-rank adaptation) fine-tune to convert generic text into my writing style, using ~20,000 words of my completed writing as training data. Only the tuned models slightly improved how close the converted texts matched my original writing (chrF (character overlap score) 65.0→67.5). The preference tuning memorized the pairs and performed at chance level.
long: The idea is a model that takes generic assistant-like writing and converts it into my writing style. I gathered 44 of my finished written documents (~20,000 words, 73 passages) and used a base model to rewrite my writing in a generic style, then trained the model to convert the generic style to my writing. The documents were divided so that the 9 evaluation passages are from 5 documents not used in training. My writing is kept private and not uploaded anywhere.

I did LoRA (low-rank adaptation) training on Qwen3.5-9B (8.7 min, one A40 GPU) and QLoRA (quantized 4-bit LoRA) on Qwen3.8-27B (29.6 min). They were scored using chrF (character n-gram F-score compared to my original text, higher is more similar), where the generic text unchanged is 65.0. The base models shifted the text away from my writing (57.1 and 56.3), and even with 3 of my passages as examples they only got to 62.1 and 63.5. Only the tuned models moved it closer: 67.5 (9B) and 67.2 (27B). This is +2.5 over doing nothing, which is small as expected for only ~20,000 words of training data, and the two model sizes are tied with 9 evaluation samples. The tuned models also reduced em dashes to zero, matching my writing style.

Then I attempted DPO (direct preference optimization) using 74 of my own A/B ratings of tuned rewrites. It achieved 100% reward accuracy on the 64 training pairs but only 50% (chance) on the 10 held out: it memorized but did not learn any generalizable patterns, so I shelved that approach.

The current step is using an AI-text-detector as the reward instead of human ratings. My first probe was Pangram (commercial AI-text-detector), it rated generic drafts 1.00 (definitely AI), my rewrites after tuning 0.84 on average, and my own writing 0.08. Two rewrites of the same draft will often have very different scores (1.0 and 0.0) so pairs from the same model do have a signal to train on, with checks to make sure all facts/numbers survive the rewriting process.
highlights: chrF (character n-gram F-score): input 65.0, base model 56-57, few-shot 62-64, tuned 67.2-67.5
27B QLoRA (quantized low-rank adaptation) trains in 29.6 minutes on one 48 GB GPU
DPO (direct preference optimization) v1: 100% train, 50% held-out: memorized, shelved
AI-detector probe: drafts 1.00, tuned rewrites 0.84, my writing 0.08
